author: Michael Larabel
description: All of the SoC updates were recently merged for the ongoing Linux 7.1 kernel cycle. Most of the activity as usual is on the Arm side but also with some RISC-V additions too for the Linux 7.1 kernel...
title: Linux 7.1 Adds Support For 12 New SoCs, Other ARM & RISC-V Hardware

author: Michael Larabel
description: Over the past number of months there has been a steady flow of Intel open-source projects archived on GitHub amid the corporate restructuring at the company and realigning of their open-source focus. This week another batch of Intel open-source projects were formally archived...
title: Intel Ends Open Ecosystem Community/Evangelism, Archives Other Open-Source Projects

author: Michael Larabel
description: Ahead of tomorrow's Ubuntu 26.04 LTS release, Canonical published a blog post today outlining the state of Rust Coreutils for its premiere in this long-term support (LTS) version. Canonical also commissioned a security audit recently of Rust Coreutils that turned up 44 CVEs and 113 issues in total...
title: Ubuntu Rust Coreutils Audit Revealed 113 Issues, Ubuntu 26.10 Aims For "100% Rust Coreutils"

author: Michael Larabel
description: GCC 16.1 as the first stable version of the GCC 16 compiler is nearly ready for its official debut as this year's major feature release for this open-source compiler...
title: GCC 16 Compiler Nearly Ready For Release With Zen 6, AVX10.2, APX & Algol 68

author: Michael Larabel
description: FreeBSD is out today with their Q1-2026 status report to outline the many different development initiatives their open-source developers have participated in over the past quarter. There is a lot of hardware enablement efforts ongoing as well as continuing to make a more compelling desktop experience and also improving GUI and management options for FreeBSD systems...
title: FreeBSD Working On Intel FRED Support, Laptop Improvements Continue

author: Michael Larabel
description: KMSCON 9.3.4 is out today for this virtual terminal (VT) emulator in user-space that runs atop the Linux DRM/KMS APIs for those wanting to enjoy a CONFIG_VT=n Linux kernel experience...
title: KMSCON Continues Improving For VT Terminal Emulator In User-Space

author: Michael Larabel
description: Merged recently to Linux Git were the big set of networking changes for the Linux 7.1 kernel...
title: Many Great Networking Improvements Arrive In Linux 7.1

author: Michael Larabel
description: Canonical is out with a new blog post today outlining toolchain changes to Ubuntu Linux from Ubuntu 24.04 LTS to Ubuntu 26.04 LTS due for release tomorrow. While those changes over the past two years aren't too news worthy if you have been following the interim Ubuntu releases, what's interesting is their road ahead on the Ubuntu toolchain front for developers...
title: Ubuntu Looks Toward More Snap-Based Devpacks Moving Forward

author: Michael Larabel
description: As part of Intel's LLM-Scaler initiative for AI inferencing on Intel Arc hardware, out today is their vllm-0.14.0-b8.2 update that includes officially supporting the Arc Pro B70 graphics card...
title: Intel LLM-Scaler vllm-0.14.0-b8.2 Released With Official Arc Pro B70 Support

author: Michael Larabel
description: Intel today published their official quarterly feature release to their open-source Media Driver providing Video Acceleration API (VA-API) support on Linux...
title: Intel Media Driver 2026Q1 Continues Nova Lake S Enablement

author: Michael Larabel
description: Since Ubuntu 25.04 Ptyxis has been the default terminal emulator after it initially became available in Ubuntu 24.10. For the upcoming Ubuntu 26.04 LTS release, Ptyxis remains the default but Ghostty is now available too...
title: Ghostty OpenGL-Accelerated Terminal Available On Ubuntu 26.04 LTS

author: Michael Larabel
description: The QEMU 11.0 emulator is now available for this important piece of the open-source Linux virtualization stack...
title: QEMU 11.0 Released With CET Virtualization Support, Native Nitro Enclaves
